name: Host Header Injection (Reset Poisoning, Routing SSRF)
description: Abuses an application's trust in the HTTP Host (or X-Forwarded-Host) header. Primary impacts: password-reset poisoning (the reset link is built from the attacker-controlled host so the token is sent to the attacker), routing-based SSRF (manipulating the host to reach internal systems through the front-end), cache issues, and authentication/validation bypass via an injected or duplicated Host header.
source: PortSwigger Web Security Academy - HTTP Host header attacks
notes:
=== WHY IT WORKS ===
  Apps read the Host header to build absolute URLs (reset links, redirects) or to route requests. If that value is attacker-controlled and trusted, links point at the attacker and routing can be redirected internally.

=== PASSWORD-RESET POISONING ===
  1. Trigger a reset for the victim's email, but set Host: attacker.com (or X-Forwarded-Host).
  2. The app emails the victim a link like https://attacker.com/reset?token=... built from your host.
  3. When the victim clicks, the token hits your server -> account takeover.
  Variants: inject a second Host header, use X-Forwarded-Host, or Host: target.com:@attacker.com.

=== ROUTING-BASED SSRF ===
  - Some front-ends route upstream based on the Host header. Changing it can reach internal vhosts or the cloud metadata endpoint.
  - Try Host: 169.254.169.254, Host: localhost, or internal names; watch for different responses.

=== VALIDATION / AUTH BYPASS ===
  - Access controls keyed on Host (e.g. 'only Host: internal admin') can be spoofed.
  - Duplicate Host headers / absolute-URI request line to confuse the parser.

=== TESTS ===
  - Change Host outright; if the site still works, the header is trusted downstream.
  - Add X-Forwarded-Host: attacker.com and look for it reflected in links/redirects.
  - Use Burp Repeater; inspect reset emails / Location headers.

recommended.note: Host-header reflection is a primary unkeyed input for poisoning a cache.
Routing-based Host abuse is a path into SSRF of internal services.
Reset-poisoning is one of several password-reset takeover techniques.

defense.why_it_works: The application builds security-sensitive URLs (password-reset links, redirects) or routing decisions from the client-controlled Host / X-Forwarded-Host header, so an attacker who changes it redirects tokens to their server or reaches internal upstreams.
defense.prerequisites: An app that reflects or routes on the Host/X-Forwarded-Host header and does not validate it against an allow-list. For reset poisoning, the ability to trigger a reset for the victim's account.
defense.impact: Account takeover via stolen reset tokens, SSRF into internal services and cloud metadata, cache poisoning, and bypass of Host-based access controls.
defense.detection: [MITRE T1190] Requests whose Host or X-Forwarded-Host does not match the site's canonical domain(s), duplicate Host headers, Host values pointing at RFC1918/link-local addresses, and password-reset emails whose link host differs from the canonical host.
defense.artifacts: Reverse-proxy/web access logs capturing the Host and X-Forwarded-Host headers, mail-gateway logs of outbound reset links, and application logs of reset-token generation.
defense.splunk_spl:
index=web uri_path="/forgot-password"
| rex field=_raw "X-Forwarded-Host:\s*(?<xfh>[^\r\n]+)"
| rex field=_raw "\nHost:\s*(?<host>[^\r\n]+)"
| where (isnotnull(xfh) AND xfh!="<target>") OR (isnotnull(host) AND host!="<target>")
| stats count by clientip, host, xfh
defense.sentinel_kql:
W3CIISLog
| where csUriStem =~ "/forgot-password"
| extend host = csHost
| where host != "<target>"
| summarize count() by cIP, host
defense.prevention: Do not trust the Host header for anything security-relevant: build absolute URLs from a server-side configured canonical domain, validate Host against an allow-list and return 400 otherwise, strip or ignore X-Forwarded-Host unless set by your own edge, and bind reset tokens to the account and a fixed base URL.

detections.name: Password-reset request with off-domain Host / X-Forwarded-Host
detections.logic:
index=web sourcetype=apache uri_path="/forgot-password"
| rex field=_raw "X-Forwarded-Host:\s*(?<xfh>[^\r\n]+)"
| rex field=_raw "\nHost:\s*(?<host>[^\r\n]+)"
| where (isnotnull(host) AND NOT match(host, "^<target>$")) OR (isnotnull(xfh) AND NOT match(xfh, "^<target>$"))
| stats count by clientip, host, xfh
detections.false_positives: Legitimate alternate domains / vanity hosts the app genuinely serves.
detections.tuning: Allow-list every canonical and vanity host; alert only on reset endpoints with an unrecognized host value.
